level1.text: The coil of a school generator model has $300$ turns, and its area is $0.0030\,\text{m}^2$. The coil rotates in a uniform magnetic field of $0.15\,\text{T}$ at a rotation frequency of $10\,\text{Hz}$. How large is the peak value of the voltage induced in the coil?
The electrical system of a passenger aircraft has an alternating voltage with an rms value of $115\,\text{V}$ and a frequency of $400\,\text{Hz}$. How large is the peak value of the voltage?
The sinusoidal alternating current in the element of a kettle has a peak value of $8.5\,\text{A}$. How large is the rms value of the current?
The shaft of a hydropower plant's generator makes $1500$ revolutions per minute. How large is the rotation frequency of the shaft in hertz?

An electric heater is connected to a mains voltage with an rms value of $230\,\text{V}$, and the rms value of its current is $4.35\,\text{A}$. How large is the average power of the heater? Give the answer in kilowatts.
People say that the voltage of a household socket is $230\,\text{V}$. Which statement about this voltage is correct?
level1.answer: The number $230\,\text{V}$ is the rms value, because it produces the same power as a direct voltage.

choices.text: The number $230\,\text{V}$ is the peak value, because the meter shows the greatest instantaneous voltage.
choices.feedback: Meters do not show the peak value but the rms value, and the $230\,\text{V}$ of the socket is an rms value. The peak value of the voltage is about $325\,\text{V}$, that is, larger than the stated number.

choices.text: The number $230\,\text{V}$ is the average value, because the positive and negative voltages are equal in size.
choices.feedback: The average of a sinusoidal voltage over one period is zero, because the positive and negative values cancel each other. The number $230\,\text{V}$ is based on power, not on the average: it is the rms value.

choices.text: The number $230\,\text{V}$ is the rms value, because it produces the same power as a direct voltage.
choices.feedback: Correct: the rms value is defined through power. It is the direct voltage that would produce the same average power in a resistor, and the peak value of a sinusoidal voltage is $\sqrt{2}$ times the rms value, about $325\,\text{V}$.

choices.text: The number $230\,\text{V}$ is the rms value, because the peak value is smaller than the rms value.
choices.feedback: The number $230\,\text{V}$ is indeed the rms value, but the reasoning is wrong: the peak value of a sinusoidal voltage is larger than the rms value, about $230\,\text{V} \cdot \sqrt{2} \approx 325\,\text{V}$. The rms value is defined through power.

level1.text: The coil of a generator rotates at $3000$ revolutions per minute. How long is the period of the alternating voltage produced, in milliseconds?
The peak value of a sinusoidal alternating voltage was measured with an oscilloscope as $17.0\,\text{V}$. What voltage does a multimeter show when it measures the same voltage?

level2.text: The rectangular coil of a generator has $150$ turns, and the lengths of its sides are $6.0\,\text{cm}$ and $8.0\,\text{cm}$. The coil rotates in a uniform magnetic field of $0.25\,\text{T}$ and makes $1200$ revolutions per minute. How large is the peak value of the voltage induced in the coil?

The graph shows the voltage of a small generator as a function of time. The coil of the generator has $200$ turns, its area is $30\,\text{cm}^2$, and it rotates in a uniform magnetic field. Read the peak value and the period of the voltage from the graph. How large is the magnetic flux density?

A hiker charges a battery with a hand-cranked generator whose voltage must have an rms value of $12\,\text{V}$. The coil of the generator has $200$ turns, its area is $0.0050\,\text{m}^2$, and the magnetic field is $0.30\,\text{T}$. At what rotation frequency must the coil be turned?

In 2024 Finland's wind turbines produced $19.8\,\text{TWh}$ of electricity, and at the end of the year their combined rated power was $8358\,\text{MW}$ (Suomen Uusiutuvat ry, wind power statistics 2024). The year 2024 had $366$ days. What percentage of the rated power at the end of the year was the average power of the wind turbines?

An oscilloscope measured the voltage $e$ of a small generator as a function of time $t$, and the measurements are in the table (sample data). The voltage is sinusoidal, and the data points cover more than one period.

a) Deduce the period and frequency of the voltage from the table.

b) Read the peak value of the voltage from the table.

c) Calculate the rms value of the voltage.

The result of part c is entered in the answer field.

A group investigated by experiment how the voltage of a generator depends on the rotation frequency. The coil and the magnet stayed the same, and the rotation frequency was doubled. The peak values of the voltage measured with an oscilloscope are in the table (sample data).

a) Use the formula $e_0 = NBA \cdot 2\pi f$ to predict the peak value at the rotation frequency $10.0\,\text{Hz}$ on the basis of the first measurement.

b) By how many percent does the measured peak value differ from the prediction? Calculate the deviation from the prediction and give its absolute value.

c) State how the frequency of the voltage changes, and assess whether the measurement fits the prediction when the uncertainty of reading each peak value is $\pm 0.1\,\text{V}$.

The result of part b is entered in the answer field.

level2.text:
A student solved a problem as follows: “The power of an incandescent bulb is $60\,\text{W}$, and it is connected to the mains voltage $230\,\text{V}$. The voltage is a peak value, so the rms value is $230\,\text{V} : \sqrt{2} = 163\,\text{V}$. The current is $I = P : U = 60\,\text{W} : 163\,\text{V} = 0.37\,\text{A}$.”

a) Find the error in the student’s solution and explain why it is an error.

b) Calculate the rms value of the current of the bulb correctly.

The result of part b is entered in the answer field.

level3.text: The coil of a generator rotates steadily, and the peak value of its voltage is $20.0\,\text{V}$. At the moment $t = 0$ the plane of the coil is perpendicular to the field. How large is the voltage of the coil when the coil has turned $30^\circ$ from this position?

A generator whose voltage has a peak value of $40\,\text{V}$ is connected to a $40\,\Omega$ resistor. The resistance of the generator itself is so small that it can be ignored. How large is the average power of the resistor?

In a direct-drive wind turbine a permanent-magnet generator rotates at the same rate as the rotor. The rms value of the generator's voltage is $690\,\text{V}$ when the rotor turns at $15$ revolutions per minute. The wind weakens, and the rotor now turns at only $9.0$ revolutions per minute. The magnets and coils of the generator are the same, and the frequency converter is not taken into account. How large is the rms value of the generator's voltage now?

A bottle dynamo is a small generator pressed against the side of a bicycle tyre; its coil has $240$ turns and an area of $6.0\,\text{cm}^2$. The peak value $e_0$ of the voltage of the dynamo was measured with an oscilloscope at different rotation frequencies $f$ (sample data, table).

a) Fit a straight line $e_0 = kf + c$ to the data points with the linear fit of a calculator or by eye, and determine its slope $k$.

b) Use the slope to calculate the magnetic flux density $B$, and explain why, according to the formula $e_0 = NBA \cdot 2\pi f$, the line should pass through the origin even though the measured line does not.

c) Predict the peak value at the frequency $22\,\text{Hz}$ and assess whether the constant term $c$ matters in the prediction.

The magnetic flux density of part b is entered in the answer field.

level3.text:
The coil of a teaching-laboratory generator has $120$ turns and an area of $0.0050\,\text{m}^2$. The coil rotates in a uniform magnetic field of $0.20\,\text{T}$, and the generator is connected to a resistor of $8.0\,\Omega$.

The resistance of the generator itself is so small that it can be neglected. The rotation frequency is first $25\,\text{Hz}$ and then $40\,\text{Hz}$ (sample situation).

a) Calculate the peak value and the rms value of the voltage at both rotation frequencies.

b) Calculate the average power of the resistor at both rotation frequencies, and the greatest value of the instantaneous power $p(t)$ at the rotation frequency $40\,\text{Hz}$.

c) Explain why the power grows to more than double although the rotation frequency grows only $1.6$-fold.

The average power of the resistor at the rotation frequency $40\,\text{Hz}$ is entered in the answer field.
